requirements.heading: Requirements Notation
requirements.text: When the terms "MUST", "MUST NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", and "MAY" appear capitalized, they are being used to indicate particular requirements of this specification.

requirements.heading: Requirements Notation
requirements.text: A discussion of the meanings of the terms "MUST", "SHOULD", and "MAY" appears in [RFC-1123]; the terms "MUST NOT" and "SHOULD NOT" are logical extensions of this usage.

requirements.heading: Client use of pipelining
requirements.text: Client SMTP implementations that employ pipelining MUST check ALL statuses associated with each command in a group.

requirements.heading: Client use of pipelining
requirements.text: Command statuses MUST be coordinated with responses by counting each separate response and correlating that count with the number of commands known to have been issued.

requirements.heading: Client use of pipelining
requirements.text: Client SMTP implementations MAY elect to operate in a nonblocking fashion, processing server responses immediately upon receipt, even if there is still data pending transmission from the client's previous TCP send operation.

requirements.heading: Client use of pipelining
requirements.text: If nonblocking operation is not supported, however, client SMTP implementations MUST also check the TCP window size and make sure that each group of commands fits entirely within the window.

requirements.heading: Client use of pipelining
requirements.text: Clients MUST NOT confuse responses to multiple commands with multiline responses.

requirements.heading: Server support of pipelining
requirements.text: (1) MUST respond to commands in the order they are received from the client.

requirements.heading: Server support of pipelining
requirements.text: (2) SHOULD elect to store responses to grouped RSET, MAIL FROM, SEND FROM, SOML FROM, SAML FROM, and RCPT TO commands in an internal buffer so they can sent as a unit.

requirements.heading: Server support of pipelining
requirements.text: (3) SHOULD issue a positive response to the DATA command if and only if one or more valid RCPT TO addresses have been previously received.

requirements.heading: Server support of pipelining
requirements.text: (4) MUST NOT, after issuing a positive response to a DATA command with no valid recipients and subsequently receiving an empty message, send any message whatsoever to anybody.

requirements.heading: Server support of pipelining
requirements.text: (5) MUST NOT buffer responses to EHLO, DATA, VRFY, EXPN, TURN, QUIT, and NOOP.

requirements.heading: Server support of pipelining
requirements.text: (6) MUST NOT buffer responses to unrecognized commands.

requirements.heading: Server support of pipelining
requirements.text: (7) MUST send all pending responses immediately whenever the local TCP input buffer is emptied.

requirements.heading: Server support of pipelining
requirements.text: (8) MUST NOT make assumptions about commands that are yet to be received.

requirements.heading: Server support of pipelining
requirements.text: (9) MUST NOT flush or otherwise lose the contents of the TCP input buffer under any circumstances whatsoever.

requirements.heading: Server support of pipelining
requirements.text: (10) SHOULD issue response text that indicates, either implicitly or explicitly, what command the response matches.
